FreeDOS Is 23 Years Old, and Counting

I have nothing but good memories of FreeDOS. Back in... somewhere between '96 and '98... I set up an old 486DX2/66 with FreeDOS and nothing but free software, to find out if DOS was still a viable OS choice. And I succeeded.

It had Vim, GNU tools, ispell, TeX, and a converter for most commercial word processor file formats, for word processing. Lynx, Pine, and some ftp and telnet clients for the internet*. A simple paint program, and an image viewer and converter for all formats I ever came across. It could even play mp3, mpeg video, and most avi files.

Shit, it would still be a viable home computer, if modern web developers had not decided to shit on the idea of an open hypertext web, and fuck everything up with layers upon layers of pointless JavaScript.

Edit: *: I used the shell account** on my ISP's HP Unix machine for IRC. And a non-free, but very popular, terminal program and a local BBS for Usenet and other BBS networks.

**: They did not even advertise it as such. Creating a normal user account for each client, and then starting a ppp session was just the easiest way they could come up with to offer their service. Back then nobody really worried about security. I even called them about it, and they said it was perfectly fine to use my account as I see fit. It even had a really generous storage quota, because nobody ever used it.
